title: Introduce contextual SLO quieting and signal deduplication
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: During the capacity regression on 2026-02-20 we observed a large number of pages caused by transient token-level burn spikes from multi-tenant workloads. The current burn-rate alerting aggregates signals across routes and regions and emits separate page events for each distinct aggregation window. This produced noisy, duplicate pages for the same underlying incident and drove unnecessary on-call fatigue.

Goal: Reduce paging noise and duplicate alerts while preserving sensitivity to real regressions. Implement a set of coordinated changes: (1) signal deduplication layer that collapses similar alerts within a short contextual window, (2) a decay-weighted burn normalizer to reduce the impact of short-lived spikes on burn-rate thresholds, and (3) incident-aware quieting rules that prevent repeated pages after an alert has already been paged and acknowledged. All changes should be configurable per-SLO and enabled in shadow mode for 2 weeks before enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deduplication collapses >= 90% of duplicate pages in the 5-minute window in canary test; 2) Shadow mode produces an SLI dashboard showing reduced page count without changing routing for 14 days; 3) No missed high-severity regressions in simulated tests; 4) Rollout plan documented and rollback switch available via console; 5) New metrics added: deduped_pages_count, normalized_burn_value, quiet_window_hits.
implementation_notes:
Design choices: use deterministic grouping key = hash(route||model||region||tenant_bucket) and a sliding window of 30s for dedup collapse. Normalizer algorithm: exponential decay with half-life 60s applied to burn contributions so brief spikes contribute less to burn-rate. Quieting: once a page for a grouping key is fired and acknowledged, suppress further pages for that key for 10 minutes unless severity escalates.

Trade-offs: longer quiet windows reduce noise but increase risk of missing subsequent failures for the same key; we choose conservative defaults (30s dedup, 60s half-life, 10m quiet) and will tune. Complexity: needs a small state store for active grouping keys; prefer in-memory LRU sharded by route with periodic persistence to redis if eviction rate gets high.

Testing plan: unit tests for grouping/dedup logic, integration test using load generation harness, and chaos tests that simulate flapping tenants. Shadow run for two weeks with dashboards and pager counts compared to baseline.
